title: Pressed Proof
description: A case study. Red errors scold and flash. These fields show validity in the weight, the ink, the rule, and a deboss you can see.
problem: Red error states scold and flash, and color-only feedback fails for anyone who cannot see that red.
interaction: A typical red form sits beside the pressed field. Unfinished type stays light, on a thin rule. A valid value jumps in weight, ink, rule, and a visible deboss. An error is a dashed rule, a sentence that says how to fix it, and one small wobble.
technique: A custom element, pressed-field, with the input in light DOM so a native form still submits and validates. Fraunces SOFT and wght carry the impression. Fonts without those axes fall back to weight, ink density, and the rule. Events pp:valid and pp:invalid.
ship: The element in a lead form: email, name, WhatsApp, submit. Drop the before column, the preset switcher, and the knobs. Keep the weight, the rule, the deboss, the sentence, one wobble, and an instant cut when reduced motion is on.

title: Material Picker
description: One twisted, five-lobed form in three contemporary finishes: prism glass, gummy candy, and flock.
problem: A material swatch is a flat chip. It cannot show how a finish bends light, glows, or eats it until you see it on a form.
interaction: Pick Prism glass, Gummy, or Flock from a small dock. The object swaps material while the poster behind it recolours and spells the finish. It turns slowly on its own; drag to turn it.
technique: three.js r186 MeshPhysicalMaterial on a hand-built twisted superformula mesh, lit by a Poly Haven HDRI. Glass uses transmission, dispersion, and thin-film iridescence over a canvas-texture poster, so the black type splits into spectra. Gummy uses attenuation, sheen, and a view-dependent thickness tweak. Flock uses sheen and a generated fibre normal map.
ship: Rough preview. A real configurator would load the product mesh, keep the dock and the backdrop that recolours with the finish, and drop the poster word on small screens if it competes.

title: Flute Clear
description: Craft beer cans behind fluted glass. Hover, scroll, or tap a card and the ribs clear, then price and CTA fade in.
problem: A product grid shows every card at full volume, so nothing tells you which one you are looking at.
interaction: Each photo sits behind ribbed glass, so only stripes of colour show. Hover clears the ribs and the price and CTA fade in. On touch, the card nearest the middle of the screen clears as you scroll, and a tap toggles it.
technique: Paper Shaders FlutedGlass (@paper-design/shaders) on a WebGL canvas per card, eased out on hover or keyboard focus. An IntersectionObserver picks the centred card on phones. Unsplash photos.
ship: Rough preview. In a shop: one shared canvas or a CSS fallback for long grids, and product photos shot on consistent backdrops so the stripes read as one family.

title: Magnetic Weight Nav
description: A vertical menu whose words get heavier and wider as the pointer or finger draws near.
problem: A static menu gives no hint which item you are about to choose.
interaction: Each word's weight and width track pointer or finger distance. The nearest word turns signal blue.

title: Hi-Vis After Dark
description: A headlamp in the dark. Retroreflective lettering stays dull grey until the beam lines up with your eye.
problem: The word, the tape, the cone bands, and the sign stay dull grey until the lamp sits next to the camera. The return should collapse when the lamp slides off that axis, even though the light still hits the letters.
interaction: Move the pointer, or drag on a touch screen, to steer the camera a little and aim the beam. Click, or tap without dragging, to flash. Headlamp offset is the control that kills the glow.
technique: three.js r186 MeshPhysicalNodeMaterial retroreflectivity. The specular lobe is evaluated with the view direction reflected about the normal, so it only fires when the lamp and the eye line up. WebGPU, with a WebGL2 fallback when WebGPU is missing or only partial.
ship: One alignment control on a flat wordmark. A still frame when reduced motion is on, and no camera flash in that mode.

title: Hello WebGPU
description: A full-screen animated fragment shader running on WebGPU, with a WebGL2 fallback.
problem: A full-bleed hero background has to keep running on machines that do not have WebGPU.
interaction: Nothing to steer. The shader plays on its own. If WebGPU is missing or fails to start, the same picture comes up through WebGL2.
technique: One full-screen triangle. A WGSL fragment shader on WebGPU, and the same loop in GLSL ES 3.0 on WebGL2. Pixel ratio capped at 2.
ship: Use it behind real content. Pause the loop when reduced motion is requested, and treat the WebGL2 path as the one phones will actually hit.
